export function mountOnboarding(): void {
  const sheet = document.querySelector(".sheet");
  const main = document.querySelector("main");
  const puzzleEl = document.getElementById("puzzle");
  if (!sheet || !main || !puzzleEl) return;

  const forced = FORCED[new URLSearchParams(location.search).get("state") ?? ""];
  const anyNamedState = new URLSearchParams(location.search).has("state");
  // Design's named states must screenshot without this layer; only onboarding's own states show it.
  if (anyNamedState && !forced) return;

  document.head.appendChild(Object.assign(document.createElement("style"), { textContent: STYLE }));

  // One strip between the title block and the two pictures: the first-run guide (dismissible),
  // then the always-available explainer and the hint slot. Never covers the controls.
  const strip = document.createElement("section");
  strip.id = "onboarding";
  strip.setAttribute("aria-label", "Guide");
  strip.innerHTML = FIRST_RUN + TRACE_EXPLAINER;
  main.before(strip);
  const firstRun = strip.querySelector<HTMLElement>(".first-run")!;
  const details = strip.querySelector("details")!;
  const hintEl = strip.querySelector<HTMLElement>(".hint")!;

  let dismissed = false;

What changed - Left rail: title, calibre, puzzle picker, then the job card with symptom, goal and hold bar, then the first-run guide and hints under it. - Centre: the movement drawing fills the whole column, with the speed slider on top. - Right: the timegrapher, with the adjustment sliders in a two-up grid directly under it and the true-rate readout below. - One window, no page scroll at 1100px wide and above. Checked at 1440×900, 1280×800 and 1280×720. If a rail's content runs long, such as the open guide, that column scrolls on its own. - Narrower screens: mid widths put the job strip across the top with movement and instrument side by side. Phones stack job, instrument, sliders, then movement.
